items.evidence: Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself
items.note: The student correctly defines recursion as a function calling itself.

items.evidence: Every recursive solution requires at least one base case
items.note: The student states that a recursive function requires at least one base case.
The student mentions stopping the process but does not clearly explain that the base case returns a result without making further recursive calls.

items.evidence: to solve smaller instances of the same problem
items.note: The student explains that recursive calls operate on smaller instances of the problem.

items.evidence: Each function call gets its own separate set of local variables and parameters pushed onto the call stack
items.note: The student explains that each call pushes an independent set of variables onto the call stack.
The student mentions preventing infinite loops but does not specifically state that an absent or unreachable base case triggers a stack overflow error.
The student did not mention that any recursive algorithm can be rewritten iteratively.
The student did not mention tail call optimization.

target_reason: Understanding that recursion and iteration are computationally equivalent is important for choosing the right approach.
